Title
 Standard Test Method for 
 Phosphorus in Water

Colorimetric Molybdovanadophosphate Method 
 in Water 
 Using ASTM D 515-79 ( Method C )

This method covers the routine determination of 
 dissolved orthophosphate in water. It is best suited to boiler feedwater and 
 boiler water containing 1 to 10 mg/liter ( ppm ) of phosphorus. The range can 
 be extended upward by diluting the sample.

The first draft was initiated by chemist: Wafaa 
 Esmail; reviewed by department director chemist: Zakia Soltan; revised by 
 quality control chemist: Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel and accepted by Eng. Awad M. 
 Fatthy; Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.

Phosphorus is widely 
 distributed in the environment as both inorganic and organically bound 
 phosphates. Sources of phosphates include surfaceapplied fertilizers, 
 cleaning and laundering products, boiler water conditioners, and drinking 
 water treatment aids. Because phosphorus is a nutrient for photosynthetic 
 organisms, it may be important to monitor and control discharge into the 
 environment.

This method is based on the photometric 
 measurement of yellow color of molybdovanado-phosphoric acid developed in 
 the sample. The color intensity is proportional to the orthophosphate 
 concentration of the sample.

This method is not suitable for highly colored 
 waters, such as tannin-treated boiler water, unless the color is first removed. 
 High concentrations of ferric ions interfere with this test, but generally aren't present in the waters for which the method is intended.

When determining only dissolved phosphorus in boiler waters, filter the sample 
 through a 0.45 m membrane filter to remove particulate matter as soon as 
 possible after sampling. Delay in the filtration may alter the 
 relationship between the dissolved and particulate forms of phosphorus. Since 
 membrane filters may contain significant amounts of phosphorus, they should be 
 washed prior to use.

Analysis is best performed immediately after collecting 
 the sample to minimize possible change. If analysis can't be performed the 
 same day is collected, preserve the sample by adding 40 mg/l HgCL2 
 to sample and refrigerating it at 4C. To prevent precipitation of the 
 mercury, add sufficient NaCL to the sample, if necessary, so that it will have 
 a chloride content of at least 50 mg/l.

Collect the 
 sample in accordance with method D 3370-76, Grab 
 Samples.

The reagent 
 used must be of sufficiently high purity to permit its use without 
 lessening the accuracy of determination.

 length of the solution being measured. The range can be more than doubled by 
 measuring the color at a wavelength from 470 to 490 nm instead of from 400 to

items:
Ammonium MolybdateVanadate Solution 
 Dissolve 40 gm of ammonium molybdate [ ( NH4 )6 MO7O24. 
 4H2O ] in 400 ml of water. Dissolve 1.0 gm of ammonium 
 metavanadate ( NH4VO3 ) in a mixture of 300 ml of 
 water and 200ml of concentrated nitric acid ( HNO3, spgr 1.42 ). 
 Add the first solution to the second solution, mix, and dilute to 1 liter 
 with water.

Phosphorus Standard Solution-( 1 ml 
 = 0.025 mg of phosphorous ) first prepare a stock solution ( 1.0 ml = 0.05 
 mg of phosphorus ) by dissolving in water 0.2197g of potassium dihydrogen 
 phosphate ( KH2PO4 ) that has been dried for 1hour in an 
 oven at 105C, and diluting the solution to exactly 1 liter with water. Prepare the 
 standard solution by diluting 50.0 ml of the stock solution to 100 ml with 
 water in a volumetric flask.

Transfer 50 ml of a clear sample ( filter 
 if suspended matter is present ) into an Erlenmeyer flask.

If the sample contains more than 10 mg / 
 liter ( ppm ) of phosphorus, use a correspondingly smaller sample diluted to 
 50 ml with water.

Add 25 ml of ammonium molybdate-vanadate 
 solution to the sample and mix well.
Allow 2 minutes for the color development.

Measure the color absorbance at 400 to 420 
 nm with a filter photometer or at 400 nm with a spectrophotometer, using 
 water as the reference sample.

Record the phosphorus concentration 
 indicated by the calibration curve prepared which cover the range from 0 to 
 10 mg/liter ( ppm ) of phosphorus. Note: A separate 
 calibration curve must be made for each photometer. Each curve must be 
 checked periodically to ensure reproducibility.

Prepare the standards by diluting suitable 
 volumes of standard phosphorus solution ( 1 ml = 0.025 mg of phosphorus ) to 
 50 ml with water.

One milliliter of phosphorus standard 
 solution diluted to 50 ml produces a standard containing 0.5 g / liter of 
 phosphorus.

Develop the color and measure the absorbance 
 at 400 to 420 nm with a filter photometer or at 400 nm with a 
 spectrophotometer, using water as the reference solution.

Plot the absorbance values obtained as 
 ordinates and the corresponding phosphorus concentrations as abscissas.
